findings.title: TOCTOU race can truncate a concurrently created file
findings.evidence: The new existence check is followed by an open in write mode, so two concurrent claim_path calls for the same path can both see it missing and the later open truncates the file created by the first caller; the prior open with exclusive-create was atomic.
findings.recommendation: Restore an atomic exclusive create, e.g. open(path, 'x') or os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY), and translate the resulting FileExistsError if needed.

findings.title: Dangling symlink bypass when base is writable by another user
findings.evidence: os.path.exists follows symlinks and returns False for a dangling symlink; the subsequent write-mode open then follows that link and creates or truncates its target. This is reachable when another user can place a symlink under base, and the old exclusive-create open rejected symlinks.
findings.recommendation: Use O_CREAT|O_EXCL (or open(path, 'x')) so existing symlinks are rejected, or open with O_NOFOLLOW where appropriate.

findings.title: Manual FileExistsError loses errno and filename contract
findings.evidence: The previous open raised FileExistsError with errno EEXIST and filename populated; the new manual raise only sets args, so callers inspecting errno or filename break.
findings.recommendation: Let the atomic open raise the error, or raise FileExistsError(errno.EEXIST, os.strerror(errno.EEXIST), path).
